note: The accept corpus is consumed in TWO directions: tests/model/*.test.js feeds it to Health.js as input, and tests/test_unifi_status.py asserts it as normalize.py output. That is what stops the Python producer and the JS consumer inventing two shapes from the same prose (risk R-F, and the mechanism by which DEV-1 went unnoticed).

attempted_at_malformed.note: A timezone-less timestamp. Accepting it would silently reinterpret the helper's clock as local time.

attempted_at_too_early.note: attemptedAt is 40 minutes before service launch. DATA-008a makes this the ONE rejection that re-baselines and retries once, because it is the signature of a laptop resuming with a slow RTC rather than a bad helper. A second consecutive one is a genuine protocol error.

bound_exceeded.note: A 513-character site name, one past the 512-char string bound.

bound_exceeded_clients.note: 501 clients listed, one past CLIENTS_LISTED_MAX, with the count raised to match for the same reason.

bound_exceeded_devices.note: 201 devices listed, one past DEVICES_LISTED_MAX. The COUNT is raised to match, so the array bound is the only thing that can reject this — `list_exceeds_total` must not be what fires.

bound_exceeded_ports.note: A device with 65 ports, one past PORTS_PER_DEVICE_MAX.

bound_exceeded_radios.note: A device with 9 radios, one past RADIOS_PER_DEVICE_MAX.

byclass_offline_mismatch.note: byClass.down + byClass.impaired is 2 while offlineTotal says 0.

byclass_sum_mismatch.note: byClass sums to 4 while devicesTotal says 5. Constructed by mutating a valid envelope, because counts() refuses to build it — which is the point: the generator asserts the invariant, so only an explicit mutation can violate it.

data_schema_violation_client_connected_a.note: A client whose `connectedAt` is an epoch NUMBER rather than a string. Checked as a string and deliberately not against the RFC 3339 grammar: the type is what DATA-B02 declares, and `formatInstant` already renders an unparseable instant as "unknown" — rejecting a whole reading over an unusual-but-valid timestamp would be the consumer enforcing more than the contract says.

data_schema_violation_client_no_id.note: A client whose `id` is the empty string.

data_schema_violation_client_type.note: A client whose `type` is null. Unrecognised types are accepted on purpose (a client type decides nothing); a MISSING one is not, because the row has nothing to render.

data_schema_violation_device_class.note: A device whose `class` is "flapping", outside REQ-000's five.

data_schema_violation_device_detail_abse.note: A device with NO `detail` key at all. Absent and null are different statements — 'the producer forgot' versus 'the producer did not ask' — and only the second is acceptable, so the key is required and its value is nullable rather than the other way round.

data_schema_violation_device_firmware_up.note: A device whose `firmwareUpdatable` is the STRING "false". This is DEV-7's own story: `!!"false"` is true, so a consumer using truthiness reports a firmware update on the strength of a word, and three mutations to `!!` survived the whole suite because every value the contract allows agrees with `=== true`.

data_schema_violation_device_metrics.note: A device whose `metrics` is a number. `detail` had a fixture for this shape and `metrics` did not, so half the check was unexercised.

data_schema_violation_device_name_number.note: A device whose `name` is a number — the nullable-string check, which six device fields and six client fields share.

data_schema_violation_device_no_id.note: A device whose `id` is absent. Named in DATA-008's row and unfixtured until now — the check existed and nothing exercised it.

data_schema_violation_device_role.note: A device reporting a role outside the three REQ-009 counts.

data_schema_violation_device_state_null.note: A device whose `state` is null. DATA-B01 marks it NON-nullable and nothing enforced that — the one field in the group where `null` is not merely the wrong type but a value the contract forbids outright.

data_schema_violation_missing_class.note: counts.byClass omits `impaired`. Absence must never be read as zero.

data_schema_violation_wan_status.note: wan.status is "flapping", outside the four-value domain.

envelope_not_object.note: The top-level JSON value is an array.

envelope_unknown_key.note: A tenth top-level key. Unknown keys are rejected rather than ignored, so a future protocol cannot be half-read by an old consumer.

error_http_status_forbidden.note: kind `credential` carrying httpStatus 429. The spec's own example: it is rejected as malformed_response, NOT acted on as a rate limit. Acting on it would let a bad envelope steer the scheduler.

error_http_status_typed_as_http.note: kind `http` carrying 401. DATA-007 requires a received status to keep its TYPED kind, so 401 must be `unauthorized` and never `http`.

error_retry_after_forbidden.note: kind `timeout` carrying retryAfterSec, which only rate_limited may.

error_retryable_mismatch.note: kind `credential` claiming retryable: true. The kind is fatal, so this would turn a permanent misconfiguration into an endless poll.

list_exceeds_total.note: Six devices listed while devicesTotal says 5. A bounded array may be SHORTER than its total — that is what the bound is for — but never longer. Longer means the total is understating the site, which is the one thing REQ-010's independent-count rule exists to prevent.

list_exceeds_total_clients.note: Two clients listed while counts.clients says 1. The same rule on the other array; `counts.clients` is nullable, so the check must not fire when it is null — success_optional_gaps is the fixture that proves it does not.

meta_helper_version_missing.note: meta.helperVersion is null. It is the ONE field DEV-2 does not make nullable.

nonce_mismatch.note: A well-formed envelope carrying a nonce the service never issued. This is the shape of output from a PREVIOUS service instance after a plugin hot-reload, which an in-memory generation counter cannot detect because the reload reset it (DATA-005a).

ok_not_boolean_integer.note: ok is the integer 1. Truthiness would accept it; identity must not.

protocol_version_string.note: protocolVersion is the STRING "1". It must be the integer.

stdout_multiple_values.note: Two JSON objects on stdout. A reader taking the first would act on a half-written batch.

stdout_not_json.note: stdout is not JSON. The likely real cause is a Python traceback, which is exactly the case that must not throw.

stdout_oversized.note: A valid envelope padded past the 256 KiB stdout bound. Synthesized rather than committed so the corpus does not carry a quarter-megabyte file into every user's plugins directory.

stdout_trailing_garbage.note: A valid envelope followed by non-whitespace.

success_data_empty.note: ok: true with data: {}. This passed EVERY stated rule in the original spec draft and is why DATA-008 now requires data to satisfy the DATA-006 schema.

success_error_not_null.note: ok: true with a populated error.

success_exit_nonzero.note: ok: true paired with a non-zero exit status.

warning_shape_invalid.note: A warning is a bare string. The panel would have to parse prose, and DATA-012's {id, name} site pairs could not be carried at all.

warnings_not_array.note: warnings is null rather than an empty array.
